gaps.sentence: There was ___ fog at the airport all morning.
gaps.explanation: thick fog (or dense fog) is the standard collocation; 'strong fog' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: The crash left several passengers seriously ___.
gaps.explanation: seriously injured is the standard collocation describing bad injuries in accidents.

gaps.sentence: It's your turn to ___ care of the dog this weekend.
gaps.explanation: take care of somebody/something means to look after them.

gaps.sentence: Make sure you are fully ___ of the terms before you sign.
gaps.explanation: fully aware of something is the fixed collocation meaning knowing completely.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ a diary since she was twelve.
gaps.explanation: keep a diary is the fixed collocation for writing in one regularly.

gaps.sentence: He was so badly ___ in the fall that he needed an operation.
gaps.explanation: badly hurt is the standard collocation meaning seriously injured.

gaps.sentence: The company ___ interest on the money it borrows.
gaps.explanation: pay interest is the standard financial collocation.

gaps.sentence: Most children learn to ___ the time before they start school.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: ___ the time (read a clock)
gaps.explanation: tell the time means to be able to read a clock; it is a fixed expression.
